q: Wednesday club race, windward mark to be left to port. You are close-hauled on port tack, one hull length from the mark and inside Red, who is close-hauled on starboard tack and fetching it. You hail "Room at the mark!" Does Red have to give you mark-room?

o: No — boats on opposite tacks are never overlapped, so rule 18 cannot apply and only rule 10 decides

o: Blue — a boat entitled to mark-room keeps it until she is clear ahead or the boats separate
Blue — mark-room lasts for three hull lengths after the mark, the same distance as the zone

q: Offset mark 60 metres to the left of the windward mark, both to be left to port. q: Leeward gate, 25 knots and waves. You are clear ahead of Black as you enter the zone of the right-hand gate mark, which you intend to round. Black — a boat clear astern must keep clear under rule 12 whatever the leading boat does at the gate

q: Leeward mark to be left to port, light wind. You and Blue are running down on port tack, overlapped, with you on the outside, when Blue's bow reaches the zone. You are the leeward boat and have right of way under rule 11. Blue hails for mark-room. What must you do?

o: Nothing — as the leeward right-of-way boat you may sail your course and Blue must keep clear

Red — the overlap must exist from at least five hull lengths to count at the mark
You — but only because you are on starboard tack and Red must keep clear anyway

q: Leeward mark to be left to port, 10 knots. White's bow enters the zone clear ahead of you by about a metre; a few seconds later, still before the mark, you get an inside overlap and call for room. White sails her rounding without giving you any, and you have to brake behind her. Was White right?
a: Yes — the moment the first boat reached the zone you were clear astern, so you must give White mark-room no matter what overlap you gain later
o: No — once you are overlapped inside in the zone, the outside boat must give you mark-room
No — a lead of one metre is within the margin of error, so the boats count as overlapped
Yes — but only because White entered the zone on starboard tack and you were on port

It gives the benefit of the doubt to the boat that hailed first
It must dismiss the protest, because without witnesses no facts can be found

In a lull she rolls over you and briefly gets clear ahead, then you surge back and the overlap is re-established just before the mark. Green now says you lost your rights when the overlap broke. Is she right?

Yes — rule 18 is re-assessed every time the overlap changes inside the zone
No — but only because you were on starboard and she was on port

q: Leeward mark, Bodrum, dying breeze. You entered the zone clear ahead of Red and then slowed badly in a hole; Red, with the last of the wind, rolls up on your inside and is overlapped by half a length as you both reach the mark. She hails "Room!" Who must give what?

Neither — once a leading boat slows, rule 18 no longer applies and rule 12 decides

Nothing — with three boats overlapped the leeward boat has right of way and sails her own rounding
Mark-room to Grey only — Blue was not overlapped with you directly, only through Grey

o: You are disqualified — a windward boat always keeps clear under rule 11, and mark-room does not change that
Both boats are disqualified — you for rule 11 and Blue for rule 18, because there was contact
Blue is exonerated — a leeward boat need not give room to a windward boat under any rule

No — because mark-room never allows an inside boat to sail more than one length from the mark

Grey — a boat entitled to mark-room must sail directly to the mark and leave it at once
You — a leeward boat can alter course at a mark without any limitation at all

q: Windward mark to be left to port, 12 knots, both of you close-hauled on starboard tack and overlapped when the first of you reaches the zone; you are inside and to leeward, Blue outside and to windward. Blue says that "port–starboard" is all that matters at marks and, as you are both on starboard, she may hold her course. Which rules actually decide?
a: Rule 18.2(a)(1) and rule 11 — Blue must give you mark-room as the outside boat and keep clear of you as the windward boat
o: Rule 10 only — at a windward mark the tack is the only thing that matters
Rule 18.3 only — any boat on starboard at a windward mark is protected
No rule — two boats on the same tack at a mark may both hold their courses
why: Rule 18.2(a)(1): the outside boat at the zone gives mark-room; between overlapped boats on the same tack rule 11 also applies.

q: Leeward mark to be left to port, 22 knots. Red enters the zone clear ahead of you and broaches right at the mark, lying on her side with the spinnaker flogging for ten seconds. You are coming down fast behind her. What may you do?
a: Pass her on the outside if you can, giving her mark-room — she is still entitled to it; you may not force your way between her and the mark, and you must avoid contact
o: Sail between her and the mark — a boat that has broached has lost her mark-room
Hold your course straight at her — she must get out of your way as soon as she recovers
Round the mark on the wrong side and correct it later, as rule 28 allows
why: Rule 18.2(a)(2): the boat astern at the zone gives mark-room for as long as the rule applies; rules 14 and 22 also require avoiding a boat out of control.
